record.original_question: For a noncompact semisimple Lie group G of rank one, a discrete subgroup Γ of G, and a horospherical subgroup U of G, what are the U-ergodic Radon measures on G/Γ? In particular, are they all either carried by closed U-orbits or obtained from the harmonic-function construction?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 12 (F . Ledrappier, O. Sarig). Let G be a noncompact semisimple Lie group of rank one, Γ a discrete subgroup of G, and U a horospherical subgroup of G. What are the U -ergodic Radon measures on G /Γ? In particular , are they either carried by closed U -orbits or given by the harmonic function construction?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a noncompact semisimple real Lie group of real rank one, let $\Gamma \subset G$ be a discrete subgroup (not assumed to be a lattice), and let $U \subset G$ be a horospherical subgroup (i.e., the unipotent radical of a minimal parabolic subgroup of $G$). Consider the right action of $U$ on the homogeneous space $G/\Gamma$, which preserves the class of locally finite Borel (Radon) measures. A $U$-invariant Radon measure $\mu$ on $G/\Gamma$ is called $U$-ergodic if every $U$-invariant Borel set has either zero or locally full $\mu$-measure. Two natural families of such measures are known:

(a) measures supported on a single closed $U$-orbit in $G/\Gamma$ (giving the Haar measure on that orbit), and

(b) measures produced by the harmonic-function construction: starting from a positive $\Gamma$-invariant eigenfunction (a harmonic function with respect to a suitable Laplacian, equivalently a $\Gamma$-conformal density on the boundary of the symmetric space of $G$), one builds an associated $U$-invariant Radon measure on $G/\Gamma$ via the Burger–Roblin / Babillot–Ledrappier construction.

Classify all $U$-ergodic Radon measures on $G/\Gamma$. In particular, determine whether every such measure is either supported on a closed $U$-orbit or arises from the harmonic-function construction described in (b).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem has substantial partial progress. In rank one, Sarig proved the classification for horocycle flows on $\mathbb Z^d$-covers of compact hyperbolic surfaces, and Ledrappier–Sarig extended it to regular covers of finite-volume surfaces. Landesberg–Lindenstrauss-type results and work by Landesberg on geometrically infinite quotients (IMRN 2022) further classify horospherical Radon measures under suitable hypotheses (e.g., when the Bowen–Margulis–Sullivan measure is conservative). However, a complete classification for arbitrary discrete subgroups $\Gamma$ of a general rank-one semisimple Lie group is not yet established in full generality, so the question remains partially solved.

status_evidence.title: On Radon Measures Invariant Under Horospherical Flows on Geometrically Infinite Quotients
status_evidence.snippet: Classification of horospherical invariant Radon measures on geometrically infinite rank-one quotients under conservativity assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Partial classification results in rank one beyond the geometrically finite case.

status_evidence.title: Invariant Radon measures for horocycle flows on Abelian covers (Sarig)
status_evidence.snippet: Sarig classifies ergodic invariant Radon measures for horocycle flows on Z^d-covers of compact negatively curved surfaces, proving a conjecture of Babillot-Ledrappier.
status_evidence.claim: The classification is established in the abelian cover case.

status_evidence.title: Invariant measures for the horocycle flow on periodic hyperbolic surfaces (Ledrappier-Sarig)
status_evidence.snippet: Extends the horocycle Radon measure classification to regular covers of finite-volume hyperbolic surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: Further partial resolution for regular covers.

status_evidence.title: Horospherical invariant measures and a rank dichotomy for Anosov groups
status_evidence.snippet: Generalizes Burger–Roblin rank-one classification to higher rank Anosov subgroups.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates the rank-one problem motivates ongoing higher-rank generalizations.
